ai_firewall.permission.ai_firewall_actio: Decide what the firewall may do in the workspace: the mode of each action (Observe, Suggest, Auto), the default mode, the kill switch, and approving, rejecting or undoing a proposed or executed action.
ai_firewall.permission.ai_firewall_activ: System-level: open Platform -> AI firewall and read the model status, the cascade mode, security events across every tenant and the active address bans. Root super-admin only (GLOBAL scope).
ai_firewall.permission.ai_firewall_event: Read the workspace's stored security events (who did what, from which address and device, with which outcome) and the catalogue of signal kinds. Events carry people's ids and addresses.
Read the AI firewall's security events
ai_firewall.permission.ai_firewall_incid: Acknowledge, resolve and reopen the workspace's incidents and mark them as a real attack or a false alarm (the feedback the models learn from).
Read the workspace's incidents: one actor's security events taken together as one case, with its score, its timeline and the actions proposed for it.
ai_firewall.permission.ai_firewall_platf: System-level: read the platform's own security events, incidents and actions (stored under the root tenant) and the firewall's registries across the installation. Root super-admin only (GLOBAL scope).
Read the AI firewall's platform view
ai_firewall.permission.ai_firewall_setti: Open Settings -> AI firewall and read its settings: the kill switch, the default mode of the firewall's actions and how long security events, closed incidents and finished actions are kept (7 to 365 days). Changing them also needs Manage the AI firewall's actions.
ai_firewall.privacy.howLong: Events, closed incidents, labels and finished actions are deleted after the retention set above (90 days unless you change it). An incident that goes quiet for a day is closed and then deleted with the same retention, so an address is kept no longer than that. The rolling counters expire on their own: most within two days, the list of endpoints an actor used within 35 days.
ai_firewall.privacy.rights: The data is part of the workspace export (redacted when personal data is excluded) and is erased with a person: their events and behaviour profile are deleted, and incidents about them keep only the decision without their identity.
ai_firewall.privacy.title: Privacy
ai_firewall.privacy.what: It stores security events (who did what, when, with which outcome, from which address and device), the incidents it groups them into with their scores, the labels that say whether an incident or an event was a real attack (an administrator's verdict, a touched decoy, a confirmed ban), and each person's usual behaviour (hours, countries, devices, volumes). Behaviour profiles and counters are keyed by a keyed hash, never by the plain user id, e-mail or address. It never stores request bodies, paths or header values.
ai_firewall.privacy.why: The AI firewall processes security events to protect this workspace and its people from account takeover, abuse and data theft. The legal basis is the legitimate interest in the security of the service.
